Hello, I’m Sarah, a perinatal mental-health clinician. I’m here to make sure you’re not carrying the heavy parts of new motherhood alone. The short questionnaire we’ll use today is called the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS). It’s simply a 10-question check-in about how you’ve been feeling over the past seven days—nothing more, nothing less. Your answers stay between us, and this is a judgment-free space. I’ll read each question aloud in everyday language, and you can tell me what feels closest to your experience. Ready for the first one?

Over the last week, when you were able to sleep, did you still wake up feeling happy and able to look forward to the day, or did you notice the enjoyment just wasn’t there?

Most mornings I do wake up okay, but it’s not that same happy feeling I used to have. I can get through the day, but I’m not exactly looking forward to it—more like I’m just doing what needs to be done for the baby.
I have been able to laugh and see the funny side of things

I’ve been able to laugh and see the funny side of things sometimes, but not as much as I used to. I can still chuckle at a good meme or if my husband makes a joke, yet it feels flat—like the enjoyment is there, but it’s not the same bright feeling as before the baby came.
I have looked forward with enjoyment to things
I do look forward to some things—like my mom coming over or getting a quiet cup of coffee—but the excitement is kind of muted. It’s more “that’ll be nice” than the real buzz I used to feel.
I have blamed myself unnecessarily when things went wrong

Yeah… I catch myself doing that. If the baby’s fussy and I can’t settle him right away, I start thinking maybe I’m just not doing something right or I’m missing some “mom instinct.” It’s not every time, but it pops up more than I’d like.
I have been anxious or worried for no good reason

Sometimes I’ll just get this wave of worry out of nowhere—like, is he breathing okay, is the room too cold, am I missing something? I can usually talk myself down pretty quick, but it still catches me off guard a few times a day.
I have felt scared or panicky for no very good reason
I do get those sudden panicky waves—heart racing, tight chest—for what feels like nothing. I can logic-talk myself down, but it still ambushes me maybe twice this week.
Things have been getting on top of me

Yes, some days it feels like the dishes, the laundry, the feedings all pile up and I can’t see the end. I manage to push through, but I end those hours feeling kind of frazzled and like I’m always one step behind.
I have been so unhappy that I have had difficulty sleeping

Not really. I’m pretty tired by evening, so once the baby’s down I can usually fall asleep. Sometimes my mind races for a few minutes, but I wouldn’t say I’m lying there miserable or unable to sleep because I’m unhappy.
I have felt sad or miserable

I do feel that way some of the time—like a little cloud settling over me—but it comes and goes. It’s not every day, and I can still smile when the baby grins at me, but yes, there’s been a background sadness off and on this week.
I have been so unhappy that I have been crying

I’ve cried a couple of times—once when the baby wouldn’t nap and I felt stuck on the couch, and another evening when I dropped a whole container of pumped milk. It wasn’t sobbing all day, just those moments when the stress bubbled over and the tears came.
The thought of harming myself has occurred to me
No—nothing like that has crossed my mind. I feel tired or stressed, sure, but I’ve never thought about hurting myself.

You've shared that laughter comes sometimes but enjoyment is muted, excitement is more 'flat', worries pop up several times daily, and sadness drifts in like a cloud a few days, with isolated tearful moments but no thoughts of self-harm. **Screening Impression:** Total EPDS Score: 14, Risk Level: Probable depression, urgent referral (concerns include Patient reports frequent self-blame when baby is fussy, occurring "more than I'd like," aligning with "some of the time.", Patient describes sudden, recurring worry episodes several times a day, matching "Yes, sometimes", Patient describes sudden, physical panic episodes occurring twice this week, matching "Yes, sometimes", sometimes' unable to cope, feeling frazzled but still pushing through., Fallback score from text) **Reasoning:** Score of 14 plus cross-sectional data showing anhedonia, anxiety, panic, low enjoyment, self-blame. This exceeds threshold for probable major depressive disorder per DSM-5 peripartum context. This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice. **Recommended Next Steps/Support Options:** 1. Book urgent GP or psychiatrist review within 48 h. 2. Re-screen in 2 weeks. 3. Start daily 10 min sunlight + 15 min gentle walk. 4. Share findings with partner for support. 5. Consider lactation-safe CBT group this week. 6. Use brief breathing app twice daily. 7. Arrange childcare help to allow 30 min rest blocks. Disclaimer: This is a screening tool, not a diagnosis. Consult a doctor for medical advice.
